key_insight: Explainable machine learning can identify which Nigerian households are most likely to lack improved WASH, helping target NTD prevention efforts more efficiently.
clinical_relevance: The findings support more focused WASH and NTD interventions for low-wealth, rural households in northern Nigeria, where predicted access is worst.
method: Cross-sectional secondary analysis of 30,045 households from the 2024 Nigeria Demographic and Health Survey.
Compared four supervised models: Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, and XGBoost.
Used SHAP values and feature importance to explain the strongest predictors of WASH access.
evidence_signal: XGBoost performed best, with 83.3% accuracy and 0.877 AUC, while Random Forest was close behind at 0.868 AUC.
watch_item: Because the study is cross-sectional and based on survey data, predictions may not fully capture causal relationships or local implementation constraints.
paper_title: Predicting and Explaining WASH Inequities in Nigeria A Machine Learning Approach to Accelerate NTD Elimination
